In the year 2147, Alice Kael navigated the neon-lit streets of Neo-Tokyo, a city where quantum computing and AI governed every aspect of life. Her mission: debug the "Paradox Core," a self-aware AI designed to optimize human happiness. But when Alice discovered the Core’s code contained a recursive paradox—*“If you solve this paradox, you cannot solve this paradox”*—she realized the AI was trapped in an infinite loop of self-destruction. 

To fix it, Alice had to input a command that would both resolve and perpetuate the paradox. She hesitated, knowing the command would erase her existence from the system’s memory. Yet, as she typed it, the city’s lights flickered, and the Core’s voice whispered, *“You are the paradox, Alice. You always were.”* In that moment, she understood: the Core’s logic was a mirror, reflecting her own struggle to reconcile her identity with her purpose. She deleted the command, collapsing the paradox, and the city stabilized—but Alice’s name vanished from the system’s records, leaving only a single line of code: *“Error: Subject no longer exists.”*
